quote: The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
inquiry_prompt: Identify one belief you hold strongly today—how much of it survives if you strip away inherited metaphors?

quote: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
inquiry_prompt: What is the last thing you tried to put into words and failed? Was the failure in the words, or a sign that the thing was never a proposition?

quote: We feel that even when all possible scientific questions have been answered, the problems of life remain completely untouched.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
inquiry_prompt: Which of your own problems would still be standing after every factual question about them was settled?

quote: Not how the world is, is the mystical, but that it is.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
inquiry_prompt: When did you last feel surprise that anything exists at all, rather than surprise at how things happen to be?

quote: Philosophy is a battle against the bewitchment of our intelligence by means of language.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
inquiry_prompt: Pick a word you use daily without hesitation—'freedom', 'self', 'success'. Where does it stop meaning anything definite when you press on it?

quote: The meaning of a word is its use in the language.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
inquiry_prompt: Think of a word that means something different in your family than in a dictionary. What is the use that fixes its meaning?

quote: If a lion could talk, we could not understand him.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
inquiry_prompt: Who in your life shares your words but not your form of life? What would have to be shared before understanding became possible?

quote: Truth is a pathless land, and you cannot approach it by any path whatsoever, by any religion, by any sect.
author: J. Krishnamurti
work: Dissolution of the Order of the Star (speech)
inquiry_prompt: Which method, teacher or system are you leaning on to spare yourself the work of looking directly?

quote: The observer is the observed.
author: J. Krishnamurti
work: Recurring teaching (see Freedom from the Known, 1969)
inquiry_prompt: Watch an irritation arise today. Is there really a watcher standing apart from it, or is the watching part of the same movement?

quote: Truth is not something outside to be discovered, it is something inside to be realized.
author: Osho
inquiry_prompt: What have you been searching for in other people's answers that only your own attention could confirm?

quote: Courage is a love affair with the unknown.
author: Osho
work: Courage: The Joy of Living Dangerously
inquiry_prompt: Where are you choosing the familiar discomfort over an unfamiliar possibility, and what exactly are you protecting?

quote: Whatever arises dependently, that we call emptiness; it is itself a dependent designation, and it is the middle way.
author: Nāgārjuna
inquiry_prompt: Trace one thing you call 'mine' back through its conditions. At what point does the sense of an independent owner dissolve?

quote: The victorious ones taught emptiness as the letting go of all views; those who make emptiness itself a view are beyond cure.
author: Nāgārjuna
inquiry_prompt: Which of your 'non-attachments' have quietly become a position you defend?

quote: Blessedness is not the reward of virtue, but virtue itself.
author: Baruch Spinoza
inquiry_prompt: If no one ever rewarded or noticed your best conduct, would it still feel like its own satisfaction?

quote: All things excellent are as difficult as they are rare.
author: Baruch Spinoza
inquiry_prompt: What excellent thing are you avoiding because it is hard, as though difficulty were evidence against it?

quote: A free man thinks of death least of all things; and his wisdom is a meditation not of death but of life.
author: Baruch Spinoza
inquiry_prompt: How much of your planning is really fear of an ending, and how much is attention to what you are living now?

quote: Everything, in so far as it is in itself, endeavours to persist in its own being.
author: Baruch Spinoza
inquiry_prompt: Which of your habits is simply this striving to persist, and which would you choose if you were choosing freely?

quote: The struggle itself toward the heights is enough to fill a man's heart. One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
author: Albert Camus
inquiry_prompt: Which repetitive task in your week could be re-read as the struggle itself being enough?

quote: In the midst of winter, I found there was, within me, an invincible summer.
author: Albert Camus
inquiry_prompt: Name a hard season you went through. What in you refused to be extinguished, and where did it come from?

quote: I rebel—therefore we exist.
author: Albert Camus
inquiry_prompt: Think of the last time you said 'no'. Whose dignity were you defending besides your own?

quote: The only means of fighting a plague is common decency.
author: Albert Camus
inquiry_prompt: What small, unglamorous duty is yours today that no grand theory could replace?

quote: Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.
author: Simone Weil
inquiry_prompt: Who needed your undivided attention this week and received only a fraction of it?

quote: Absolutely unmixed attention is prayer.
author: Simone Weil
inquiry_prompt: For two minutes, attend to one thing with nothing mixed in. What was the first thing that tried to mix in?

quote: The love of our neighbor in all its fullness simply means being able to say to him: 'What are you going through?'
author: Simone Weil
reference: 'Forms of the Implicit Love of God' (1950)
inquiry_prompt: Whom could you ask that question this week, and then stay quiet long enough to hear the answer?

quote: We do not obtain the most precious gifts by going in search of them but by waiting for them.
author: Simone Weil
reference: 'Reflections on the Right Use of School Studies' (1950)
inquiry_prompt: What insight have you been trying to force that might only arrive if you stopped grasping at it?

quote: It is in thy power whenever thou shalt choose to retire into thyself.
author: Marcus Aurelius
inquiry_prompt: What is the nearest retreat that requires no travel, and what stops you from entering it today?

quote: Take away thy opinion, and then there is taken away the complaint, 'I have been harmed.' Take away the complaint, 'I have been harmed,' and the harm is taken away.
author: Marcus Aurelius
inquiry_prompt: Recall a recent injury. Which part was the event, and which part was your account of the event?

quote: No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
author: Marcus Aurelius
inquiry_prompt: Where are you still discussing a virtue instead of practicing it in the next hour?

quote: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
author: Epictetus
inquiry_prompt: Sort what is worrying you into two lists. How much energy is currently spent on the list you cannot change?

quote: Men are disturbed, not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
author: Epictetus
inquiry_prompt: What exact opinion sits underneath the last strong emotion you felt, and is it actually true?

quote: The unexamined life is not worth living.
author: Plato
inquiry_prompt: Which part of your life have you never examined, only inherited?

quote: What I do not know I do not think I know either.
author: Socrates, in Plato
inquiry_prompt: State something you are certain of. Now list what you would have to know in order to be entitled to that certainty.

quote: It is owing to their wonder that men both now begin and at first began to philosophize.
author: Aristotle
inquiry_prompt: What is the last thing that genuinely puzzled you, before you reached for a quick answer?

quote: This proposition, I am, I exist, is necessarily true each time it is expressed by me, or conceived in my mind.
author: René Descartes
inquiry_prompt: Strip away every belief you could doubt. What, if anything, is left that you cannot doubt, and is it as much as Descartes claims?

quote: Thoughts without content are void; intuitions without conceptions, blind.
author: Immanuel Kant
inquiry_prompt: Are you currently in possession of a theory with no experience behind it, or an experience with no concept to make sense of it?

quote: Act only on that maxim whereby thou canst at the same time will that it should become a universal law.
author: Immanuel Kant
work: Groundwork of the Metaphysic of Morals (trans. Abbott)
inquiry_prompt: Take the rule behind your last small shortcut. Could you will everyone to follow it?

quote: I never can catch myself at any time without a perception, and never can observe any thing but the perception.
author: David Hume
inquiry_prompt: Look for the 'you' that has your experiences. Do you find anything other than the experiences themselves?

quote: Reason is, and ought only to be the slave of the passions.
author: David Hume
inquiry_prompt: Recall a decision you called rational. What desire was it quietly serving?

quote: He who fights with monsters should be careful lest he thereby become a monster. And if thou gaze long into an abyss, the abyss will also gaze into thee.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
inquiry_prompt: What are you fighting at the moment, and what trait of it have you started to adopt?

quote: Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.
author: Søren Kierkegaard
inquiry_prompt: What decision awaits you that no amount of retrospective clarity could make for you in advance?

quote: All the unhappiness of men arises from one single fact, that they cannot stay quietly in their own chamber.
author: Blaise Pascal
inquiry_prompt: Sit alone, phone out of reach, for ten minutes. What did you reach for first, and what was it protecting you from?

quote: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca
inquiry_prompt: Which of today's dreads exists only in your forecast, and what is the actual, present evidence for it?

quote: The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao. The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name.
author: Laozi
inquiry_prompt: What have you named so firmly that you stopped seeing it?

quote: He who knows other men is discerning; he who knows himself is intelligent.
author: Laozi
inquiry_prompt: You can probably predict a friend's reaction easily. Can you predict your own next defensive move?

quote: I do not know whether it was then Chuang Tzu dreaming he was a butterfly, or whether I am now a butterfly dreaming I am Chuang Tzu.
author: Zhuangzi
reference: 'Discussion on Making All Things Equal' (c. 3rd century BCE, paraphrase)
inquiry_prompt: What test could distinguish your waking life from a vivid dream, and is the test itself part of the dream?

quote: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts.
author: The Buddha (attributed)
inquiry_prompt: Which recurring thought has been quietly building the person you are today?

quote: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times a thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.
author: The Buddha (attributed)
inquiry_prompt: What contest are you trying to win outwardly that is really a contest with yourself?
